issue.title: Two ACE PNG snapshots render the host's real launch-default model badge (CLAUDE(opus)) instead of the fixture-pinned CODEX(visual-snapshot-model)
issue.description:
DISCOVERED while landing epic sase-p1 (glossary panel); NOT caused by that epic -- no
glossary code is on the failing path and the pixel diff is confined to the top-bar
launch-default badge.

FAILING NODES (both, identical 5786 changed / 5784 material pixel signature):
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_tribe_panel.py::test_tribe_panel_display_config_png_snapshot
  tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_retry_e2e.py::test_real_fakey_completed_retry_chain_png_snapshot

SYMPTOM: the golden's top-bar badge reads `CODEX(visual-snapshot-model)`; the actual
render reads `CLAUDE(opus)`. Everything else in the frame is byte-identical. Confirmed by
cropping expected.png/actual.png at (950,50)-(1482,110) and by
`grep -o 'CLAUDE[^<]*' actual.svg` -> exactly one match, no `visual-snapshot-model`.

`CLAUDE(opus)` is exactly this host's live value:
  .venv/bin/python -c "from sase.llm_provider.temporary_override_defaults import \
    resolve_effective_default_provider_model as r; print(r())"  ->  ('claude', 'opus')
so the badge is leaking real host config into a snapshot the fixture is supposed to pin.

REPRODUCTION (workspace sase_16, master d4594a416 + one unrelated PNG golden change):
  just test-visual tests/ace/tui/visual/test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_tribe_panel.py::test_tribe_panel_display_config_png_snapshot
  -> 1 failed, three times in a row, serially, in isolation (not xdist contention).
The retry-e2e node failed in two consecutive full `just test-visual` runs. The tribe node
passed in the first full run and failed in the second and in every isolated run since, so
the leak is at least partly timing/host-state dependent.

WHAT I RULED OUT (so the worker does not redo it):
- Not renderer/font drift (cf. sase-dl): the diff is a text change, not antialiasing, and
  max_diff_ratio is 0.0 outside the badge.
- Not xdist contention (cf. sase-dc / sase-ol): reproduces serially and in isolation.
- Not an unpatched fixture: tests/ace/tui/visual/_ace_png_snapshot_startup.py
  `patch_startup_loaders` monkeypatches BOTH resolution paths on the
  `sase.ace.tui.widgets.llm_override_indicator` module itself --
  `resolve_effective_default_provider_model` (lines 261-265) and
  `build_launch_model_setting_snapshot` (lines 276-280) -- and asserts at lines 297-300
  that the first one actually bound. `peek_active_temporary_override` is patched to None,
  and the host has no active override.
- Both tests call `patch_startup_loaders(monkeypatch, ...)` before entering `AcePage`.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE WORKER: every code path in
src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/llm_override_indicator.py that can populate `_cached_default`
funnels through one of those two patched callables (`_build_default_content` at line 284,
or the thread worker at lines 148-168 whose result is stored at line 113), yet the real
host value reaches the screen. Find the path that escapes the patch. One unpatched real-
host reader is on the tick path: `peek_launch_default_change_token()`
(src/sase/llm_provider/launch_default_peek.py) stats the live rotation-state, provider-
disable, and temporary-override files plus `current_config_token()`, so on a busy host it
can fire `_schedule_default_resolution_if_needed()` repeatedly during a snapshot --
a plausible entry point for the race, and worth pinning in the visual fixture regardless.

IMPACT: `just test-visual` is red for every agent on this host for two nodes that have
nothing to do with the diff under test, and the goldens are only correct on a machine
whose configured launch default happens to match the pin.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-dl — retired/canceled umbrella for broad ACE PNG baseline drift. This bead is explicitly NOT that: the diff is a two-word text change in one badge, not a repo-wide antialiasing signature.

RELATED: sase-dc / sase-ny — prior owners of the four test_ace_png_snapshots_agents_retry_e2e.py nodes (contention flakiness and stale-golden rebaselining respectively, both closed). test_real_fakey_completed_retry_chain_png_snapshot is one of those four, so check their history before rebaselining rather than re-recording the golden.
